instruction: Add sliding windows and running statistics to more_itertools, next to the existing running_median. (1) running_mean(iterable, *, maxlen=None) gets the same maxlen keyword as running_median: None means all values seen so far; a positive integer means the mean of the last maxlen values (the window grows up to maxlen at the start). (2) New running_min(iterable, *, maxlen=None) and running_max(iterable, *, maxlen=None), exported from more_itertools (and in __all__): the smallest or largest of the values seen so far, or of the last maxlen values. list(running_min([4, 3, 7, 0, 8, 1, 6, 2, 9, 5], maxlen=3)) == [4, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2]. (3) New running_statistics(iterable, *, maxlen=None), exported likewise, yields one more_itertools.Stats per input value, describing the values seen so far or the window: size (how many values it covers), minimum, median (as running_median), maximum and mean (as running_mean). For [4, 3, 7] the third item equals Stats(size=3, minimum=3, median=4, maximum=7, mean=14 / 3). Stats is also exported; it is a frozen dataclass with slots and fields size, minimum, median, maximum, mean in that order: instances compare by value and are hashable, have no instance __dict__ (vars() raises TypeError), refuse attribute assignment (AttributeError), and support neither len(), indexing nor iteration (TypeError). For all four functions a non-positive maxlen raises ValueError, maxlen=1 yields values equal to the input for min, max and mean, a maxlen longer than the input gives the unbounded results, and results equal the builtin min/max and statistics.mean/statistics.median of each window. running_statistics raises immediately when called, not when first iterated: TypeError for a non-iterable argument, ValueError for a non-positive maxlen. They support int, float, Decimal and Fraction; complex values raise TypeError in running_min, running_max and running_statistics (running_mean still accepts them). Add tests.
